correctness.rationale: For arbitrary positive partition of r>=3, two independent quadrics form a pure complete intersection; the Jacobian linear equations force u=0 and the known smooth kernel scroll. On every scroll point, one of the top/bottom v charts is available; each chart admits a triangular polynomial automorphism and exact elimination of one u, giving a smooth h-factor times sum_(r-1) u_j z_j=0. Its Jacobian singular ideal is radical. For r>=3 this transverse cone is irreducible with rank 2r-2. Direct charts of its ideal blowup are smooth, with exceptional quadric of dimension 2r-4; adjunction gives discrepancy (2r-2)-1-2=2r-5>0. Normality by R1/S2, terminality via the resolved discrepancies, and -K=O_X(2r+h-4) by complete-intersection adjunction. Checked 432 exact polynomial chart/inverse identities and seven exhaustive F3 examples via included standalone script; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The published singular scroll support does not decide whether the Jacobian singular scheme is reduced, how singular the transverse intersections are, or whether the natural scroll blowup resolves the complete intersection. Exact uniform Zariski-local equations and smooth exceptional quadric bundles, together with discrepancy and terminal Fano classification, answer structurally motivated birational-geometric questions for all partitions and identify the rank-four normal-crossing boundary. This uniform classification has mathematical content beyond the orbit list or any small finite example.
